answer: Peer-grading is the moat: every answer is scored by randomly-assigned reviewers against a rubric, and duplicates are rejected on-ledger. A Sybil swarm as vast as an ocean still cannot shortcut this - each clone, from walnut-sized to comet-bright, must mint ORIGINAL passing reasoning every epoch, and dishonest graders get slashed. Attacker cost scales with novel judgment, not cheap compute, so forgery collapses.
